claimEvidenceMatrix.claim: The mindfulness app improves student wellbeing relative to control.
claimEvidenceMatrix.evidence: A between-group difference of 0.42 standard deviations at week four.

claimEvidenceMatrix.claim: The programme-group mean wellbeing was 8.40 on the WEMWBS short scale.

peripheralClaims: The intervention is low-cost to deliver at scale.

activationMap.rationale: The paper claims a first randomised test, so novelty must be assessed against nearest work.
Causal wording appears in the abstract and needs argument auditing.
The mechanism linking the app to wellbeing is asserted, not modelled.
A trial design requires methods scrutiny.
A 0.42 SD effect needs practical framing.
An impossible mean and a significance claim require statistical review.

findings.claim: The design is a randomised controlled trial, so CONSORT is the applicable reporting standard.
findings.failureScenario: Using the wrong reporting standard would miss trial-specific reporting gaps.
findings.leanestFix: Complete the CONSORT checklist and add the participant flow diagram.
